original_title: Transgender Military Ban: Thousands of Troops Discharged for Gender Identity

existing.title: Transgender Military Ban: Thousands of Troops Discharged for Gender Identity
existing.description_short: Transgender Military Ban: Thousands of Troops Discharged for Gender Identity
existing.description_long: On January 27, 2025, President Trump signed Prioritizing Military Excellence and Readiness, an executive order reinstating the transgender military ban and directing the discharge of all transgender service members. The order declared that expressing a false gender identity divergent from an individual's sex cannot satisfy the rigorous standards necessary for military service. The order revoked Biden's Executive Order 14004, which had allowed transgender service members to serve openly and receive transition-related care. A federal judge initially blocked the ban as unconstitutional, but on May 6, 2025, the Supreme Court's 6-3 conservative majority allowed the ban to take effect while legal challenges continued — clearing the way for thousands of transgender troops to be discharged. The Department of Defense was directed within 60 days to update medical standards to bar those with gender dysphoria, end invented and identification-based pronoun usage, and prohibit shared facilities based on gender identity. Simultaneously, the State Department suspended all passport applications requesting sex-marker changes, and the administration issued a government-wide executive order declaring the U.S. government recognizes only two sexes.

In Portland on October 2, 2025, Frank Miranda, a California-born U.S. citizen, was approached by masked, unidentified plainclothes officers who told him he was 'on an overstay' before detaining him for hours. Alvarado and seven other Americans filed joint legal claims alleging wrongful detention and racial profiling; their attorney stated agents were 'stopping, detaining, arresting, putting people in federal custody and then asking questions later.'

original_title: Radio Free Europe and Radio Free Asia Grants Terminated

existing.title: Radio Free Europe and Radio Free Asia Grants Terminated
existing.description_short: Radio Free Europe and Radio Free Asia Grants Terminated
existing.description_long: On March 15, 2025, simultaneous with the VOA shutdown, the Trump administration terminated federal grants to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL), Radio Free Asia (RFA), and the Middle East Broadcasting Networks. RFE/RL had been founded in 1950 to counter Soviet propaganda and broadcasts to countries including Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, and Central Asia. RFA broadcasts to China, North Korea, and Southeast Asia. RFE/RL president Steve Capus said the termination would be a massive gift to America's enemies, many of whom are already celebrating. RFA president Bay Fang called it a reward to dictators and despots, including the Chinese Communist Party. Czech Republic Foreign Minister Jan Lipavský immediately sought EU backing to maintain RFE/RL operations from its Prague headquarters. USAGM's funding terminations had Kari Lake's signature. A senior official at one of the networks told NPR: We would bleed out. Prior funding freeze attempts during Trump's first term had been halted by courts. Russian and Chinese state propaganda celebrated the grant terminations. The combined networks had reached over 420 million people weekly across more than 100 countries in 63 languages.

A judge blocked Khalil's deportation on March 10, and he remained in a Louisiana detention facility as of late March 2025 — detained solely for his political speech.

original_title: DOJ Demands All 2024 Wayne County Michigan Ballots in Swing State Power Play

existing.title: DOJ Demands All 2024 Wayne County Michigan Ballots in Swing State Power Play
existing.description_short: DOJ Demands All 2024 Wayne County Michigan Ballots in Swing State Power Play
existing.description_long: On April 14, 2026, Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon sent a letter to Wayne County, Michigan — home to Detroit and nearly 865,000 votes cast in 2024 — demanding that the county turn over all 2024 election ballots, ballot receipts, and ballot envelopes within 14 days, threatening court action for non-compliance. The request cited the Civil Rights Act of 1960 but justified the demand using fraud allegations from the 2020 election, even though the request was for 2024 records from an election Trump won. Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel vowed to fight the demand, and county officials noted the county did not actually hold custody of the ballots. FBI Director Kash Patel said the DOJ was probing past elections and could soon make arrests, amplifying the intimidation. The Wayne County demand came weeks after the FBI seized 700 boxes of 2020 Fulton County, Georgia, ballots and subpoenaed 2020 records from Maricopa County, Arizona. Legal experts described the escalating demands as a coordinated strategy to intimidate election workers in heavily Democratic, majority-minority counties in swing states ahead of the 2026 midterms.

Analysts warned that withholding air defense interceptors in particular — while Russia ramped up mass drone campaigns against civilian infrastructure — was a de facto strategic gift to Moscow at the cost of Ukrainian civilian lives.

existing.description_short: Supreme Court Grants DOGE Unimpeded Access to Social Security Records
existing.description_long: On June 6, 2025, a 6-3 Supreme Court granted the Trump administration's emergency request to lift a lower-court preliminary injunction that had blocked DOGE from accessing sensitive Social Security Administration records. The unsigned majority order provided no detailed reasoning. Liberal justices Sotomayor, Kagan, and Jackson dissented. The ruling came after U.S. District Judge Ellen Lipton Hollander of Maryland had found in April 2025 that the government never identified or articulated even a single reason for which the DOGE Team needs unlimited access to SSA's entire record systems, exposing personal, confidential, sensitive, and private information that millions of Americans entrusted to their government. Several DOGE staffers had been granted access to SSA systems — including the Master Beneficiary Record, Supplemental Security Record, and Numident files — before their background checks were completed and before inter-agency detail agreements were finalized. DOGE staffer Akash Bobba had been working off-site at OPM while accessing SSA's master data warehouse, creating additional exposure risks.

original_title: Tariffs Add $17,000 to New Home Costs, Deepening Housing Crisis

existing.title: Tariffs Add $17,000 to New Home Costs, Deepening Housing Crisis
existing.description_short: Tariffs Add $17,000 to New Home Costs, Deepening Housing Crisis
existing.description_long: Trump's tariffs delivered a direct blow to America's pre-existing housing affordability emergency. CoreLogic estimated in March 2025 that tariffs on Canada, Mexico, and China would increase new home construction costs by 4%–6%, adding $17,000–$22,000 to the price of a typical new home averaging $422,000. Canada supplies 85% of U.S. softwood lumber imports — nearly a quarter of total domestic supply — and Trump doubled the existing 14.5% tariff on Canadian softwood lumber to 35% by late 2025. A 50% tariff on imported kitchen cabinets, 30% on upholstered furniture, and 25% on heavy construction trucks were announced for October 2025. A study found tariffs could add $26,000 in Oklahoma to over $100,000 in Hawaii per home. Single-family housing starts fell to a near 2.5-year low in August 2025, and permits dropped to levels not seen since April 2023. The National Association of Home Builders estimated each additional $1,000 in construction costs priced out 115,000 potential homebuying families. This directly contradicted Trump's stated goal of making housing affordable again. The Yale Budget Lab projected construction output would decline 3.6% in the long run due to tariffs.

original_title: DOGE Bypassed Security Protocols on Three Treasury Payment Systems, GAO Finds

existing.title: DOGE Bypassed Security Protocols on Three Treasury Payment Systems, GAO Finds
existing.description_short: DOGE Bypassed Security Protocols on Three Treasury Payment Systems, GAO Finds
existing.description_long: A Government Accountability Office audit released in April 2026 confirmed that two DOGE associates gained access to Bureau of the Fiscal Service (BFS) payment systems from January 20 through April 11, 2025, without following proper IT security protocols. The GAO found that one DOGE employee could view, copy, and print data from three BFS systems, and was inadvertently granted temporary access to create, modify, and delete data for one system. The staffer sent personally identifiable information on 350 USAID payment recipients to another DOGE staffer via an unencrypted Excel file using a Treasury email, then forwarded the unencrypted file to two DOGE members at the General Services Administration without approval. The BFS had not implemented all required cybersecurity controls. One DOGE staffer left the agency while still holding an interim security clearance enabling access to multiple BFS systems, because BFS never conducted an exit interview or obtained post-employment protection documentation. The GAO issued six recommendations for remediation. Treasury agreed with only three. The watchdog concluded that payment data remained at a greater risk of improper access, modification, disclosure, or misuse until proper controls were established.

original_title: FCC Forces ABC to Suspend Jimmy Kimmel Over Charlie Kirk Monologue

existing.title: FCC Forces ABC to Suspend Jimmy Kimmel Over Charlie Kirk Monologue
existing.description_short: FCC Forces ABC to Suspend Jimmy Kimmel Over Charlie Kirk Monologue
existing.description_long: On September 17-18, 2025, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr appeared on a conservative podcast and threatened to revoke ABC affiliate broadcast licenses if they continued airing Jimmy Kimmel Live! — citing Kimmel's Monday monologue suggesting Trump supporters were exploiting the death of Charlie Kirk. Within hours of Carr's threats, Nexstar Media Group (operator of 28 ABC affiliates, with its $6.2 billion Tegna merger requiring FCC approval) announced it would preempt the show indefinitely. Sinclair Broadcast Group (38 ABC stations, also with pending FCC regulatory matters) followed. ABC parent Disney, which was seeking FCC approval for ESPN's NFL Network acquisition, then suspended Kimmel indefinitely. Trump called it Great News for America. FCC Democrat Anna Gomez said Disney had faced clear government intimidation. The ACLU, Writers Guild, SAG-AFTRA, and dozens of lawmakers condemned the suspension as government-compelled censorship. After protests in California and national outcry, Disney reinstated Kimmel on September 22. CBS had canceled The Late Show with Stephen Colbert under comparable circumstances months earlier, also coinciding with its $16 million Trump settlement and FCC merger approval. Both Colbert and Kimmel were TV's two most vocally anti-Trump late-night hosts.

original_title: DOGE-SSA Employees Sign Secret Voter Data Agreement with True the Vote

existing.title: DOGE-SSA Employees Sign Secret Voter Data Agreement with True the Vote
existing.description_short: DOGE-SSA Employees Sign Secret Voter Data Agreement with True the Vote
existing.description_long: In March 2025, two DOGE staffers embedded at the Social Security Administration were contacted by a political advocacy group widely identified as True the Vote seeking to analyze state voter rolls using SSA data to find evidence of voter fraud and to overturn election results in certain States. One DOGE staffer signed a Voter Data Agreement on March 24, 2025, in his capacity as an SSA employee without the knowledge or approval of SSA leadership or review through proper data exchange procedures. The arrangement was not discovered until November 2025, when an internal SSA audit uncovered it. The SSA made two Hatch Act referrals to the U.S. Office of Special Counsel in late December 2025. The Trump administration admitted to these facts in a January 16, 2026, court filing in a lawsuit by the AFL-CIO. Separately, DOGE staff shared SSA data through an unapproved third-party Cloudflare server and transmitted a password-protected file containing personal information on roughly 1,000 individuals to senior DOGE adviser Steve Davis. SSA whistleblower Charles Borges alleged that DOGE staffers also copied a dataset of more than 300 million Americans' information into an unsecured cloud server.

original_title: ABC Pays Trump $15M Over Stephanopoulos Comment, Sets Chilling Precedent

existing.title: ABC Pays Trump $15M Over Stephanopoulos Comment, Sets Chilling Precedent
existing.description_short: ABC Pays Trump $15M Over Stephanopoulos Comment, Sets Chilling Precedent
existing.description_long: In January 2025, Walt Disney Co., parent of ABC News, agreed to pay $15 million to Trump's presidential foundation plus $1 million in legal fees to settle a defamation lawsuit filed by Trump against anchor George Stephanopoulos. Stephanopoulos had inaccurately described the verdict in E. Jean Carroll's civil lawsuit against Trump during a live broadcast. Despite the legal case being considered weak by media law scholars — as Carroll had indeed won a civil judgment finding Trump liable for sexual abuse — Disney chose settlement over litigation, issuing a note of regret. Legal experts told outlets including TIME that the settlement would produce a chilling effect, incentivizing self-censorship across newsrooms fearful of costly litigation from a sitting president with regulatory power over their broadcast licenses. Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression chief counsel Bob Corn-Revere said: A cold wind just blew through every newsroom. The precedent set by both the ABC and CBS settlements — that networks would pay millions rather than defend accurate or defensible journalism — marked what press freedom advocates called a structural shift toward corporate capitulation to government pressure, particularly when FCC regulatory approvals were simultaneously in play.

existing.title: RFK Jr. Directs CDC to Rewrite Website Falsely Claiming Vaccines May Cause Autism
existing.description_short: RFK Jr. Directs CDC to Rewrite Website Falsely Claiming Vaccines May Cause Autism
existing.description_long: On November 19–20, 2025, RFK Jr. personally directed the CDC to rewrite its vaccine safety webpage, replacing the long-standing scientific consensus with language stating: The claim vaccines do not cause autism is not an evidence-based claim because studies have not ruled out the possibility that infant vaccines cause autism. The page further claimed health authorities had ignored studies supporting a link. AP News, Reuters, NBC News, and the Washington Post reported widespread outrage from public health experts, autism researchers, the World Health Organization, and dozens of medical societies. Sen. Bill Cassidy — who had voted to confirm Kennedy after Kennedy promised not to undermine vaccine confidence — posted that Kennedy's action was wrong, irresponsible, and actively makes Americans sicker. Kennedy later told the New York Times he had personally directed the change. The CDC's own cited Danish 2025 study of 1.2 million children actually found aluminum in vaccines was not associated with neurodevelopmental disorders — the opposite of what the page implied. Critics noted the CDC cherry-picked discredited studies while omitting the 2015 and 2021 analyses most directly rebutting the vaccine-autism claim. The WHO reissued its statement affirming vaccines do not cause autism.

existing.description_short: Trump Bible, Sneakers, and Merchandise Grift: $1.3M in Bible Royalties Alone
existing.description_long: Trump's second presidential term built on a pre-inauguration merchandise empire that generated millions in personal revenue. Trump's 2024 financial disclosure revealed he earned $1.3 million from Bible endorsement royalties in 2024 — income from the God Bless the USA Bible, co-branded with country singer Lee Greenwood and sold for $59.99-$99.99 per copy, with special Presidential and Inauguration Day editions at the higher price. Royalties flowed through CIC Ventures LLC, of which Trump was listed as manager, president, secretary, and treasurer. The same entity licensed his name for $399 Never Surrender High-Top sneakers unveiled at SneakerCon in Philadelphia in February 2024, which sold out within hours. Additional products included Trump-branded cologne (Victory47 at $99), trading card NFTs that generated at least $700,000 for the Trumps, and a Trump guitar. During his second term, new Bible editions were added endorsed by First Lady Melania Trump and Vice President JD Vance. Collectively, Trump's merchandise operation — conducted while he was a sitting legal defendant facing 91 criminal counts — was widely characterized by ethics experts as unprecedented exploitation of a political brand. The Bible in particular drew mockery: the Lincoln Project called it his latest grift.

original_title: Leo Garcia Venegas: US Citizen Detained Three Times in ICE Racial Profiling Stops

existing.title: Leo Garcia Venegas: US Citizen Detained Three Times in ICE Racial Profiling Stops
existing.description_short: Leo Garcia Venegas: US Citizen Detained Three Times in ICE Racial Profiling Stops
existing.description_long: Leo Garcia Venegas, a U.S. citizen and Alabama construction worker, was detained by immigration agents three separate times through May 2026. The first incident in mid-2025 involved agents tackling him while he filmed his brother's arrest at a construction site, ignoring his citizenship claims. A few weeks later, an officer at a home he was building refused to trust his Alabama REAL ID — which only citizens and legal residents can obtain. Videos went viral; Garcia Venegas testified before Congress and filed a federal lawsuit. Despite the pending lawsuit, he was detained a third time in May 2026. The same week, masked agents in the Bronx tackled an American teenager who, once identified as a citizen, was left bloody and bruised in an unfamiliar neighborhood. ProPublica reported that in response to its coverage, ICE official Todd Lyons acknowledged citizen detentions serve as a deterrent. His attorney argued the stops constitute racial profiling stops based on the Supreme Court's fall 2024 ruling permitting stops partly based on apparent ethnicity, job in construction, and speaking Spanish. Despite three documented detentions, ICE denied his damage claim in April 2026 with no explanation, then detained him again two weeks later.

original_title: Courts Find DOGE Probationary Firings Illegal; 25,000 Workers Reinstated

existing.title: Courts Find DOGE Probationary Firings Illegal; 25,000 Workers Reinstated
existing.description_short: Courts Find DOGE Probationary Firings Illegal; 25,000 Workers Reinstated
existing.description_long: By mid-March 2025, two federal judges had found the Trump administration's mass firing of probationary federal workers — totaling approximately 24,583 terminations across civilian agencies — to be illegal. On March 13, U.S. District Judge William Alsup in San Francisco issued a preliminary injunction covering employees at the Departments of Veterans Affairs, Agriculture, Defense, Energy, Interior, and Treasury, calling the firings a sham because the Office of Personnel Management had orchestrated them using a template letter falsely attributing terminations to individual performance. Alsup noted that a USDA earth sciences employee had been fired after receiving only outstanding performance reviews. Hours later, U.S. District Judge James Bredar in Maryland ordered reinstatement at 18 additional agencies. Court filings showed the IRS chief human capital officer had been told by her Treasury supervisor that 6,700 firings must take place because OPM ordered them — something she described as unprecedented in her decades of federal HR work. The administration reinstated approximately 24,570 workers but placed most on administrative leave rather than returning them to duty, which Alsup explicitly said violated his order. Multiple agencies argued reinstatement would cause significant turmoil, revealing the administration's continued resistance to judicial authority over its illegal workforce dismantling.
